precepts.label: Genesis 27:40
precepts.why:
Zillah bare “Tubal–cain, an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron”: Tubal-cain designed weaponry. Then Lamech, of the same line, boasts to his wives: “I have slain a man to my wounding, and a young man to my hurt. If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold.” Anyone who tries to avenge himself on Lamech, he will rain hellfire on them. That line through Cain is the lineage that comes back again as Esau, and it was given the art of weaponry.

So Isaac’s word over Esau fits: “Behold, thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above; And by thy sword shalt thou live, and shalt serve thy brother”. By his weaponry he lives. He was to serve his brother, but his skill with the sword would be so great that “when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck.” He breaks the yoke his brother had over him.

And the principalities, the powers, the thrones he rules through were all created by Christ. Edom’s might comes from the one who made him.

That is the war we are in. Isaiah 14 calls him Lucifer and the king of Babylon: “how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!” He weakens the nations through war, and “smote the people in wrath with a continual stroke”, mostly God’s people. We have watched it: a whole country’s defense taken down and its president taken out in thirty minutes, jets shot out of the sky in ninety-three seconds, sonic weapons that left soldiers bleeding without a bullet fired, as in Panama in the eighties, and DARPA always twenty years ahead. They changed the Department of Defense back to the Department of War, because they know a name matters, as we should know the name of Israel matters.

Our people see that power and think he must be God, or that God must be with him. That is the great war of ignorance. Revelation 13 asks what the world asks: “Who is like unto the beast? who is able to make war with him?” But his pride has deceived him: “I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the most High.” He will fall, and when these devils fall, “The whole earth is at rest, and is quiet: they break forth into singing.”

precepts.label: Isaiah 54:16
precepts.why:
“Behold, I have created the smith that bloweth the coals in the fire, and that bringeth forth an instrument for his work”. Who created Cain, Lamech and Esau? Christ did. He gave them the ability to have dominion and power, principalities, spiritual wickedness in high places.

That is why the class went first to Genesis 4, where Tubal-cain was “an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron”. Isaiah, prophesying of the days to come, speaks of that same smith: the maker of weapons that began with Tubal-cain and Lamech.

Then the verse goes further: “and I have created the waster to destroy.” There is the smith, and there is the waster. An arrow, a dart, a knife or a sword does not destroy by itself; the waster destroys. God made the one who forges the weapon and the one who uses it to lay waste.

So when Edom builds Space Command in Huntsville and calls it Rocket City, when his weaponry is twenty years ahead of anything we know, remember Christ said he created the smith and the waster. “Babylon, the glory of kingdoms” draws every nation that wants a piece of the American dream, and the dragon gives power to the beast: the devil himself gives power to the beast, the white man. “And it was given unto him to make war with the saints, and to overcome them: and power was given him over all kindreds, and tongues, and nations.” Even that power was given him.

Our war is not according to flesh and blood. His weapons are not only for fighting other nations; they are to force white supremacy into our minds and spirits, until most of our people in the four corners of the earth worship the white man, even in congregations where everyone looks like them. But the Lord reminds us that they are men and not God, and their pride is the thing that brings them down.

precepts.label: Luke 17:32
precepts.why:
The angels pulled Lot into the house and smote the men at the door with blindness, and even blinded they wearied themselves trying to find the door. Then the angels took Lot out and gave them one order as the cities burned: don't look back. “And he overthrew those cities, and all the plain, and all the inhabitants of the cities, and that which grew upon the ground.” “But his wife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.”

Why would she look back? The city was being destroyed; she had just seen what happened in front of her house. She should have been glad to escape. Somebody was not vexed with the filthy conversation of that city; there was something in it she missed. That is why Luke also says, if you put your hand on the plow and look back, you are not worthy.

Christ said it in three words: “Remember Lot’s wife.” That is a warning for all of us: don't look back. You are in this truth now. Stop worrying about the long-lost cousin and auntie, stop trying to be friends with everybody and please people, stop dropping by the house on their birthday. Focus on this truth and stay away from filthiness, or be destroyed just as Lot's wife was destroyed.

Judgment is coming to Esau, as Sodom's came. “Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues.” We have to come out of her mentally, come back to the law, statutes and commandments, stop playing around in the truth, and keep the faith of Christ, without looking back.

precepts.label: Ephesians 4:28
precepts.why:
“Let him that stole steal no more: but rather let him labour, working with his hands the thing which is good, that he may have to give to him that needeth.” If you get blessed, it is to have to give to him that needeth. That is biblical, and that is part of the wisdom of Deuteronomy 4:6: the laws, statutes and commandments, everything written in the scripture, are our wisdom and our understanding, and we are to govern and deal with each other based on what God says.

How is that giving set up? You read it in Acts 2 and Acts 4: you put it at the feet of the leadership, and the leadership distributes as there is need. The leaders in the body initiate everything by the scripture, with the fundraising initiatives and the different offices, so that the body can be self-sustaining.

But many of us were raised in this environment and have not sharpened our senses, so we conduct business like Esau. Israelite businesses pop up, market to the body and make money off the body, and never come back and say, my pockets have gotten filled, my business has become profitable, I want to give back. Some even have cutthroat tactics, with no type of respect, moving the same way the world moves.

Those who say they are businessmen should read how the economics in Israel functioned and how we dealt with each other. Debt was forgiven every seven years so that debt would not pass from generation to generation. There was no usury, meaning no interest. Today what people wind up leaving behind is debt, and their families become responsible for it.

So the righteous way is to labour, prosper, and give back to the needy among our people. That is the foundation for seeing how Babylon, Esau and the rest of the world move in buying and selling, and why a nation that keeps God's statutes would be called “a wise and understanding people.”

precepts.label: Hosea 12:7
precepts.why:
“He is a merchant, the balances of deceit are in his hand: he loveth to oppress.” That spirit was in Israel as well, and this is spoken to us. Hosea deals primarily with the northern kingdom, with Judah mentioned in the mix.

Where did we learn it? Not from our own law. When you read the law and how we handled economics amongst ourselves, there was no such thing. We were mixed among the other nations and took on their customs: not only their lewdness and fornications, but how they would have no compassion on their people and how they dealt with them.

Usury was something we were supposed to do to the other nations: we lent to them and charged them interest. When we dealt with each other it was different. Not that you did not make a profit, but there were ways we dealt with each other, always with the intent that we would have communal wealth, so that generations would not get stuck with bad habits. We looked out for each other, the same way the corners of the field were left to help one another, and we were still able to prosper under that.

Instead we took up the insatiable appetite of the nations, having to get every last drop. Not so with God. That is why these balances of deceit were spoken against us. Keeping the statutes, dealing righteously with our brethren, is the wisdom Deuteronomy 4:6 says the nations will one day see in us.

precepts.label: Amos 8:5
precepts.why:
“When will the new moon be gone, that we may sell corn? and the sabbath, that we may set forth wheat, making the ephah small, and the shekel great, and falsifying the balances by deceit?” That is messing with the scales. It is the same spirit of deceitful balances read in Hosea 12:7, and it was spoken against us because we had mixed among the other nations and learned it from them.

Remember when Nehemiah had to curse out the merchants from the other nations because they came to sell on the sabbath. If we had all been in the spirit, would he have had to curse them out? We would not have bought, and they would not have come. They came because we were breaking the law by buying.

We should not have that spirit, but now you see who really does. One of the grand ways they falsify the balances today is with the oil: they call Venezuela's crude too heavy, while it is more profitable to them than anything else.

It reaches into the mortgage too. Interest is designed to keep you in debt and keep you broke, and the mortgage is loaded front heavy, so the first years go mostly to interest and not principal. On a 300,000 home a 30-year loan costs an extra 250,800, and instead of fixing the economy Trump talks about a 50-year mortgage, where you pay an additional 476,000 just to have a cheaper payment, and leave that debt to your wife and kids. That is the deceit. When we think of scales we think of the little scale at the fruit market, but this shows how broad that evil principle is. Edom does it first, and they excel at it.

It is not wrong to own a home; it is better than renting. But the system is broken and was never supposed to be that way. If our economics were set up by the law, we would lend to each other without usury and own our homes. Even to that extent the Lord had righteous weights, scales and balances, and that is the wisdom and understanding Deuteronomy 4:6 speaks of.

precepts.label: Sirach 26:19-21
precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not sow thy vineyard with divers seeds: lest the fruit of thy seed which thou hast sown, and the fruit of thy vineyard, be defiled.” Reading that, we might think only of agriculture or farming, but it is talking about much more than that, and Sirach 26 shows what.

“My son, keep the flower of thine age sound; and give not thy strength to strangers.” The strangers are the heathen, the other nations. Then it explains how you give your strength to them: “When thou hast gotten a fruitful possession through all the field, sow it with thine own seed.” A fruitful possession means you have a position, you have money, you are rich. Sow it with your own seed means sow it with your own people. You got money? Don't be going and marrying no damn white woman. What a lot of brothers do today, the first thing when they get money, is go marry a heathen. When you marry the heathen when you are rich, you are giving your strength unto strangers.

Instead, deal with your own people: start a family with the woman God created for you, “trusting in the goodness of thy stock.” Your stock is your nationality, your race, your people. You are a son of God; why would you want to go deal with other nations?

“So thy race which thou leavest shall be magnified, having the confidence of their good descent.” When you marry your sisters and bring forth children among your people, your children and your race are magnified. Good descent means your children are not confused about what their nationality is, because you did not sow your seed among all different kinds of heathen women, as our forefathers did in the book of Nehemiah.

That is the law of Deuteronomy 22:9. When we go and deal with other nations, the fruit of the vineyard is defiled: the children brought forth, the descendants, are defiled and confused.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 47:1
precepts.why:
“And after him rose up Nathan to prophesy in the time of David.” So we know who we are talking about: this is David, in the days of Nathan the prophet, the prophet the Lord sent to him after Bathsheba. The next verse carries on: “As is the fat taken away from the peace offering, so was David chosen out of the children of Israel.”

That is the same David of 2 Samuel 11. He went out on the roof, “he saw a woman washing herself; and the woman was very beautiful to look upon.” Bad to the bone. He sent and inquired: I got power, let me send some people over there, let me make this official. One with a spiritual mind made it plain: this is the wife of Uriah the Hittite, this is somebody's wife, bro. “And David sent messengers, and took her” anyway. Wisdom and understanding were right there, and he pushed them aside.

“and she came in unto him, and he lay with her”. She wasn't right either. She didn't resist, she wasn't opposed; she thought she came up. “And the woman conceived, and sent and told David, and said, I am with child.”

You see how Satan can deceive you. Satan put that lust in him to where he just didn't care, and he went the extra mile: he put Uriah in the front of the battle, got him killed, and took the wife. What he saw, the desire, the action, the cover-up, and the consequences: his first child was gone. Yet Sirach remembers David as the one chosen out of the children of Israel, and that leads to what the Lord did with him.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 47:11
precepts.why:
“The Lord took away his sins, and exalted his horn for ever: he gave him a covenant of kings, and a throne of glory in Israel.” The Lord did forgive David. He loved David, and David messed up.

David saw Bathsheba from the roof, took another man's wife, put Uriah in battle to be killed, and lost the child. That is as bad as it gets. But David repented, and the Lord took away his sins, exalted his horn, and gave him a covenant of kings and a throne of glory in Israel.

And that's another thing. A lot of times we are going to fall and do things that are not comely according to the scriptures. That don't mean you bunker down, go into a fetal position and say woe is me. You get yourself together, you repent, and you move forward. You don't go back. What did Christ say? Go, and sin no more.

You got to pick up the pieces and keep moving. We are all going to make mistakes. It is how you handle the mistake: it happened, so what are you going to do now, moving forward?

precepts.label: Ezekiel 8:14
precepts.why:
Manasseh “caused his children to pass through the fire in the valley of the son of Hinnom”. That valley, Gehenna, was where Israel burned its garbage, our refuse; the Muslims call it Gehenna, their hell. Where garbage used to be burned, they burned their children, in honor of Baal.

There was an order to it. In the spring they held orgies in honor of Ashtoreth, the fertility goddess, a black Hamite deity whose star is Venus and whose nose is knocked off the statues. Everyone slept with everyone, and the women got pregnant. Nine months later, in the winter, came the bull god, Baal, the sun god the Egyptians called Apis. The babies were laid on the plates of the brass bull with a fire under it and around it; as they burned they wiggled off into the flame, and drums were beaten to drown out their screams. That is what Manasseh was doing, by the thousands. Carnival babies, Freaknik and the club today are the same worship of that goddess.

Why sacrifice the babies? Ashtoreth gave birth to a baby god, Tammuz, and Tammuz died as an infant. The same way she lost her child, the women had to lose theirs, and the same way she wept for her child, they had to weep for the children they sacrificed on the altar. That is why Jesus is always pictured as a baby with Mary.

Ezekiel saw it: “Then he brought me to the door of the gate of the Lord’s house which was toward the north; and, behold, there sat women weeping for Tammuz.” That is what they had to do once they were in that idolatry: weep for the babies they themselves had sacrificed. And it was worse than what is brought out here.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 12:3-7
precepts.why:
“So Manasseh made Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to err, and to do worse than the heathen, whom the Lord had destroyed before the children of Israel.” Worse than the nations we were killing out of the land for doing the exact same thing. What does that mean? Wisdom of Solomon gives an idea.

“For it was thy will to destroy by the hands of our fathers both those old inhabitants of thy holy land”. Our fathers were Joshua, Caleb and the elders who succeeded Moses; when we entered the promised land we had to war with the nations already there. The old inhabitants were the Canaanites, the Hamites living in the land before we got there.

“Whom thou hatedst for doing most odious works of witchcrafts, and wicked sacrifices”: odious works are filth, evil, vile things, and that is what Manasseh was doing. “And also those merciless murderers of children”: Manasseh did it and had the people do it. “and devourers of man’s flesh, and the feasts of blood”: cannibalism, drinking blood, eating flesh. Who knows what Manasseh was doing, but he was worse than the heathen, so we have to factor this in. “and the parents, that killed with their own hands souls destitute of help”: we were killing our own kids.

“That the land, which thou esteemedst above all other, might receive a worthy colony of God’s children.” The Lord had us go in and kill those nations out of the land because they were doing these things. Then we got the land, turned around, and did the exact same thing and worse under Manasseh, as Ahab did in his time. Manasseh was one of the worst kings Judah ever had.

It had already said Manasseh “hath done wickedly above all that the Amorites did, which were before him, and hath made Judah also to sin with his idols.” He went above the Amorites; Manasseh was a monster. Chronicles gives more of the detail: he “caused his children to pass through the fire”, ancient abortions, burning his babies alive; he observed times, used enchantments and witchcraft, dealt with a familiar spirit and with wizards; he was a sorcerer. And he put an idol in the temple.

Then Kings adds what Chronicles leaves out: “Moreover Manasseh shed innocent blood very much, till he had filled Jerusalem from one end to another.” Babies on babies. That is a lot of blood, from one end of Jerusalem to the other. And it was not only him: the people did the same thing, for this was “beside his sin wherewith he made Judah to sin, in doing that which was evil in the sight of the Lord.”

Manasseh was behind a lot of death, sorcery and witchcraft; he did evil way beyond worthy of death. He killed babies, he went into witchcraft, he defiled the temple. And yet, when he was in affliction and humbled himself greatly, the Lord forgave Manasseh, heard his supplication, and put him back on the throne. The Lord has mercy on whom he will have mercy.

That is why it is so important for us to learn humility. People fall, and the Most High is able to raise them up again, like David. But don't abuse it. All of us in here ain't David; don't think, I can do what David did. No, negro, you ain't David. You're not Manasseh. You ain't Moses. The Lord puts it there to remind us that the graces and mercies of Christ were around back then too, from time to time. Don't get stupid and get prideful. Humility.

precepts.label: Sirach 6:17-18
precepts.why:
“The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul.” The law of God is perfect, it is pure, there is nothing wrong with it, and converting means to change. Only the law can change you. I used to be a murderer; the law said thou shalt not murder. I used to be a thief; the law said thou shalt not steal. I used to be an abuser. Once I know the Lord, I repent. Same thing, brother. Same thing, sister, with your trauma. Stop using your trauma as a crutch. It happened when you were 14, 15, 16, and now you're 46, 50, in your third marriage, still using it, and you can't keep a man or a woman because you cannot cope.

We never grew up around order, structure and unity. So when we come around it now, we begin to feel uncomfortable, because we realize we are the problem: the reason environments become toxic, the reason people bicker and fight, the instigating spirit we grew up seeing. Now, in a body and a truth where the light shines on that, you are forced to change, and brothers and sisters do not want to.

“Whoso feareth the Lord shall direct his friendship aright: for as he is, so shall his neighbour be also.” If you fear the Lord, you are going to direct your friendships aright, because as you are, so shall your neighbour be. But if you are constantly having issues, constantly having problems, who is the issue? Who is causing these troubles? With the laws of God and all the examples in the scriptures, you should be able to direct your friendship aright. So why is your name always in something?

“My son, gather instruction from thy youth up: so shalt thou find wisdom till thine old age.” We didn't have the opportunity to gather instruction from our youth up. But coming into this truth we have to be born again and begin to do so. You can't drag in all the ways your grandmama and your auntie and them used to deal with each other. It's a new day.

precepts.label: Sirach 6:20-21
precepts.why:
“She is very unpleasant to the unlearned.” Wisdom is very unpleasant to the unlearned. You didn't learn about yourself. All you ever did was point out other people's problems. You never examined yourself; you never looked in the mirror. So now that wisdom finally reveals who you are, it is very unpleasant.

“he that is without understanding will not remain with her.” That's why people have to find a reason to leave. They get offended, they find a reason to be mad, and then they go. What is the root cause? They don't want to change once that wisdom is revealed. And the law, which is perfect, converts only the soul that will be changed.

Destructive attitudes begin internally before they become visible externally. A person may still attend services, teach, lead, pray or serve while harboring the wrong spirit, an evil spirit. You look at the fringes and think, he's good, she's good; you would be surprised how many have an evil spirit in the midst of us. Some come here to destroy the unity of the brotherhood, because in the world it's always chaos: you never see a room full of black people with no fight, no argument, breaking bread together. Whatever you were going through in the world, you had better get over it, and quick, because that thing will destroy you. Those who carry that spirit will find themselves outside these doors.

David says it plainly: “The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.” A sacrifice for the Lord is not so much an animal. What he wants laid on the altar is a broken spirit, a broken and contrite heart, which is a broken mind.

That is the same thing Psalms 34:18 says: “The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart.” Man by nature is arrogant; we do what we want to do. So the Most High will put you in a position where he has to break you, break you down and shame you, bring you down to the lowest, until you realize: I can't do these things no more, I have to humble myself and do better, for the Lord's sake first and foremost, for my own sake, and for my people's sake as an example.

Isaiah shows where the Lord dwells when he comes near. “the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity” is the Father, and eternity is his domain, the upper room, the top floor. Yet he says, “I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite ones.” The Father and his Son deal with and dwell with the humble in spirit.

That broken spirit is the sacrifice worthy of his time. Being haughty and arrogant and offering the best sacrifices is a complete waste of time, because humility comes before honor. That is how Manasseh, a man the law said should die, found mercy: he humbled himself, and God would not despise that broken heart.

precepts.label: 1 Samuel 15:22
precepts.why:
Psalms 51:16: “For thou desirest not sacrifice; else would I give it: thou delightest not in burnt offering.” David is saying, you don’t desire sacrifice, otherwise I would give it to you; you don’t care about that either. The Lord revealed to David, I don’t care about sacrifices. And Saul didn’t listen either.

“And Samuel said, Hath the Lord as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the Lord?” Samuel is asking the question: does the Lord require sacrifices above obeying what he tells you to do?

“Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.” To hearken is to listen and humble yourself. That is better than the fat of rams.

So “The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.” The sacrifice God accepts is a broken spirit. The animals were just temporary; your mind being broken and humbled is the best sacrifice the Lord desires. You can offer and sacrifice all you want, but make sure you offer with a good heart. “Then shalt thou be pleased with the sacrifices of righteousness, with burnt offering and whole burnt offering: then shall they offer bullocks upon thine altar.” Once the sacrifices of righteousness are offered, then the bullocks on the altar become acceptable.

precepts.label: Sirach 35:17
precepts.why:
Psalms 51:17 says “a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.” Ecclesiasticus 35:17 shows what happens when the humbled one prays.

“The prayer of the humble pierceth the clouds.” It pierces the clouds: the Lord hears it. “And till it come nigh, he will not be comforted; and will not depart, till the most High shall behold to judge righteously, and execute judgment.”

That is David in Psalms 51. When Nathan confronted him after Bathsheba and Uriah, he did not stay the smartest guy in the room. He said, you are right, I am guilty: “For I acknowledge my transgressions: and my sin is ever before me.” He kept the promise he made in Psalms 32:5, “I acknowledged my sin unto thee, and mine iniquity have I not hid.” He held himself accountable, and you have to hold yourself accountable when it comes to your sins.

The bones that were broken were his humbling: being confronted with his wrong, confessing it and acknowledging it, and the consequences that followed. And out of that broken, humbled place he prayed, “Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.” That is the prayer of the humble, the one that pierces the clouds, and it is the same humility that brought mercy to King Manasseh.

precepts.label: Psalms 74:18
precepts.why:
The psalm ends its first cry with, “O God, how long shall the adversary reproach? shall the enemy blaspheme thy name for ever?” How does the enemy blaspheme? By making our signs their signs. White Jesus is blasphemy. White angels are blasphemy. All these whitewashed images are blasphemy; it is evil.

Further down Asaph says it again: “Remember this, that the enemy hath reproached, O Lord, and that the foolish people have blasphemed thy name.” The foolish people are the nations, primarily, and in some instances our own people too.

To blaspheme is to speak evil of his name, his reputation. White Jesus is blasphemy. He died for all people, the gospel is for all people, all nations can be saved: blasphemy. He isn't the son of God, he doesn't exist, I'm an atheist, evolution: blasphemy. His name is blasphemed every day all around the world.

That is why the enemy is not only the one who burned the sanctuary and the synagogues, as Babylon and Assyria did. The enemy is also the one who keeps reproaching God's name by painting over his people, so that “We see not our signs.” We don't see statues of David or Solomon or Christ as black men; we see their images, their depictions.

precepts.label: 1 Maccabees 3:48
precepts.why:
The psalm says of the enemy, “they set up their ensigns for signs.” What are their ensigns for signs? Cesare Borgia; Mother Mary, white Mary; baby white Jesus; white prophets; the Last Supper; the Sistine Chapel. Posing themselves as God, as the prophets, as the angels, as the heavenly Father: whitewashing our ensigns and making our ensigns their signs.

Maccabees shows it was done before: they “laid open the book of the law, wherein the heathen had sought to paint the likeness of their images.” The book of the law is our Bible, and the heathen sought to paint the likeness of their own images into it.

They made our signs their signs. The Greeks did it, the Romans did it, Spain did it, Portugal did it, Britain did it, the Dutch, the French: they all did it, and they still do it. It was blasphemy back then, and it is blasphemy now.

That is why Asaph cries, “We see not our signs.” The heathen painted themselves into the book of the law, and our people no longer see their own images in the scriptures that were written about them.

precepts.why:
“Blessed be the Lord my strength, which teacheth my hands to war, and my fingers to fight.” We serve a God of war, the God that formed the light and created darkness, and that God of war is Christ. David is speaking of how the Lord equipped him with his mighty fighting skills, and the same man of war teaches his soldiers to do the same. Paul says it: “Thou therefore endure hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ. No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life; that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier.”

The God of war handpicked every one of us to be soldiers in his mighty army. We are in a boot camp, a training camp, and he is teaching us how to war. Some brothers think they are here just for the unleavened bread, just to be around the brothers. No. Everything going on in the earth, in your household and in the congregation is a teachable moment, because there are spirits in all of it, and we are being built up to deal with those spirits.

It is a process. You start with yourself, subduing your own body, and that is ongoing until you go in the grave. Then your household, then the congregation, as a leader helping other brothers and sisters do the same. Even when you hear somebody else being corrected, it is about you, because at some point you will stand in that same position.

Judges shows why the nations are here: “Now these are the nations which the Lord left, to prove Israel by them”, “to teach them war.” The nations are the Lord's sword to teach us war. If you think that means go get your Glock, you are being simple. “For though we walk in the flesh, we do not war after the flesh.” At Ai the Lord said, “I have given into thy hand the king of Ai”, and still told Joshua, “lay thee an ambush for the city behind it.” The victory is already ordained, but you must go about it the way the Lord commanded. The spiritual side of the war is obedience.

So endure hardness. Some send emails saying, I am no longer with IUIC, I am going to take a break. Taking a break from the Lord? That will not work. A good soldier does not entangle himself with the affairs of this life; he stays in the fight to please the one who chose him.

precepts.label: Proverbs 16:18
precepts.why:
The first thing on the list of what the Lord hates is “A proud look.” Proverbs 16 shows where that proud look ends: “Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.”

Whenever you see somebody fall off, just know there is some form of pride in that man or that woman: something they do not want to address, an inflated ego, disdain, a haughty look, a refusal to come back to God. You might not have seen it. They might have masked it as confidence in your eyes, but God saw it as pride.

Pride is not always loud and in your face. It can be subtle: not asking for help because you do not want to seem weak, holding grudges because you feel justified, saying I am good when you are not, shutting down and thinking you do not need anybody. Pride always points the finger at somebody else and never at yourself. So when you start feeling yourself too much, puffing your chest out, say, Oh no, I am not trying to fall; let me be humble, let me be loving.

Every kingdom has failed because of pride, even ours. “Woe to the crown of pride, to the drunkards of Ephraim”: the northern kingdom fell because of pride, separating from God to do their own thing, going back to the split under Rehoboam, who would not listen to the elders. Then the southern kingdom: “After this manner will I mar the pride of Judah, and the great pride of Jerusalem.” And the warning to us: “Hear ye, and give ear; be not proud: for the Lord hath spoken.”

So the proud look is first on God’s list because it is the start of the fall. God made your eyes, your body and the mind you think with; walking in pride is departing from your maker, and it ends in destruction.

precepts.label: Romans 6:1
precepts.why:
The question put to the class: you're alone online late at night, temptation hits, and nobody from the congregation would know. What shows integrity? A, entertain the temptation privately. B, watch a little and justify it later. C, cut it off immediately and fight temptation. D, convince yourself grace covers everything. Answer D is a scary mindset to have, and Paul already answered it: “What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?”

Shall we continue in sin that grace may cover everything? That is a terrible mindset, and it is the mindset of Christianity: I found grace, grace covers me, I can do what I want when I want. All I have to do is believe in Jesus; I ain't got to do nothing he says, just believe he's my Lord and savior. Christianity is evil.

The answer is C. The questions are easy and the answers are easy; the problem is when it comes to fruition in real time. You are fighting your war against yourself: you don't want to push play, but you want to push play, and nobody is there to tell you a damn thing. That is when C gets blurred out.

The real battlefield is private. A lot of people fall spiritually in secret long before they fall publicly. The representative shows up at the Sabbath; the real you shows up at home, alone, with your family, and your wife knows exactly who you are. You can't salute so hard you're over righteous and then go home and verbally, financially or physically abuse your wife. And sisters, you can't bow 90 degrees at the door and then go home, cuss your husband out, and keep a filthy house. That is lacking integrity and poor character.

That is Proverbs 11:3: “The integrity of the upright shall guide them: but the perverseness of transgressors shall destroy them.” Grace is not a cover for sin; integrity is acting on what you know, even when nobody is watching.

precepts.label: Proverbs 17:10
precepts.why:
“He that refuseth instruction despiseth his own soul”. He doesn't want to hear it; he doesn't want to be corrected; he's always right, but wrong as hell. That isn't hurting somebody else; you are destroying your own soul, because you can't be corrected, which means you can't grow. This is why: “A reproof entereth more into a wise man than an hundred stripes into a fool.”

As a foolish person, you cannot allow wisdom to enter in. precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 1:3

Romans 15:4 says the scriptures were written for our learning; 1 Samuel 2:3 says what he does with that learning. He weighs what we do with it. Proud talk and arrogancy out of the mouth weigh nothing with him, because he is a God of knowledge and knows whether the words are backed by works.

precepts.why:

You see how stupid they are? Leaders who use this verse to say you are not going to hell are wise in their own conceits. There is a hell, and if you go against God you are going into it, Israelite or not.

So when Isaiah says “I will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians”, he is speaking of civil war in this land, city against city and kingdom against kingdom.

That is why Isaiah 19 goes on: “The Lord hath mingled a perverse spirit in the midst thereof: and they have caused Egypt to err in every work thereof.” God put a perverse spirit here, and it causes this place to be in error in everything it does. Everything that America does is in error, because there is a perverse spirit here.

You can see it in the news. Trump went to the Ford plant, a worker called him a pedophile protector, and he shot the man the bird and said “F you”. The man was suspended, and the union is fighting to get him off suspension. Somebody called out the perverse spirit, and even when they are shown their errors, they flip you the bird and make sure you lose your job.

thread.text: Woe to the crown of pride, to the drunkards of Ephraim, whose glorious beauty is a fading flower, which are on the head of the fat valleys of them that are overcome with wine!

classes.title: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.label: Jeremiah 13:9-17
precepts.why:
Every kingdom on earth has failed because of pride, even ours. Isaiah says “Woe to the crown of pride, to the drunkards of Ephraim”: the northern kingdom fell because of pride. They separated from God, went to the north and said, we are doing our own thing. It goes back to the split between Rehoboam and Jeroboam. Rehoboam could have listened to the elders who were already there to run the nation correctly, but he mocked the leadership above him and dealt with his buddies, and we are in the condition we are in today because of that pride.

The northern kingdom was the first to fall, but the southern kingdom was not exempt. “Thus saith the Lord, After this manner will I mar the pride of Judah, and the great pride of Jerusalem.” Judah looked at what their brother was doing and followed right after their treacherous sister Israel. The great pride of Jerusalem takes in Benjamin and Levi too: all of the southern kingdom was full of pride in God's eyes.

“This evil people, which refuse to hear my words, which walk in the imagination of their heart, and walk after other gods, to serve them, and to worship them, shall even be as this girdle, which is good for nothing.” When pride comes, you separate yourself from your maker, as Sirach 10 says, and walk after your own heart. When you are full of pride you are good for nothing in God's eyes.

Then the judgment for it: “And I will dash them one against another, even the fathers and the sons together, saith the Lord: I will not pity, nor spare, nor have mercy, but destroy them.” Pride destroyed the kingdom, and it destroys every kingdom.

“Hear ye, and give ear; be not proud: for the Lord hath spoken.” You better listen up, Israel, and not separate yourself from him. He is our creator and he controls all of this, so you better humble yourself and do as he tells you. This could be over right now if all of us said, Lord, I'm done with pride, I humble myself, what do you want me to do? And Christ would crack the sky.

But not on the surface, saying forgive me and then waiting till you get out of here. You are not fooling God. That is why we are still here as a people: even those of us that repented are not ready to go back to the kingdom yet. And pride is not always loud. It can be subtle, shutting down, thinking you can do it on your own, and Satan still has you there.

precepts.label: Isaiah 37:21-38
precepts.why:
Pride destroyed every kingdom on the earth, and Assyria is the first king in line. Sennacherib took all the defenced cities of Judah, then sent Rabshakeh, his herald, with big words: “What confidence is this wherein thou trustest?” When Hezekiah's men begged him to speak in the Syrian language so the people on the wall would not hear, he said he was sent to “the men that sit upon the wall, that they may eat their own dung, and drink their own piss with you.” Then he mocked the Lord himself: “Hath any of the gods of the nations delivered his land out of the hand of the king of Assyria?” … “that the Lord should deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?” All that pride came out of the king of Assyria's mouth by way of his messenger.

God heard all that smack. “Thus saith the Lord God of Israel, Whereas thou hast prayed to me against Sennacherib king of Assyria: This is the word which the Lord hath spoken concerning him; The virgin, the daughter of Zion, hath despised thee, and laughed thee to scorn; the daughter of Jerusalem hath shaken her head at thee.” She is laughing at this man's tough talk, the way a parent shakes their head when they told you not to do it and are about to whoop your ass. You are not going to one-up God, and that goes for everyone making videos mocking God's prophets. God will one-up you.

“For I will defend this city to save it for mine own sake, and for my servant David’s sake. Then the angel of the Lord went forth, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians a hundred and fourscore and five thousand.” One of God's angels destroyed 185,000. The sun went down and they were all alive; at the crack of the morning, “they were all dead corpses.” Talking prideful against God, everybody had to die.

But God was hunting Sennacherib himself. “So Sennacherib king of Assyria departed, and went and returned, and dwelt at Nineveh.” He thought he got away. Then “as he was worshipping in the house of Nisroch his god”, his own sons “smote him with the sword”, and they escaped into Armenia, and his other son Esarhaddon reigned in his stead and didn't even care.

Pride destroyed the king of Assyria, as “a man’s pride shall bring him low” in Proverbs 29. And it is the same line through every kingdom after him, Babylon, the Greeks, Rome and America: none is exempt from pride, and none is exempt from God destroying them for it.

God surnamed us, and even though he revealed himself to us and delivered us numerous times, we kept turning our backs on him. “I am the Lord, and there is none else, there is no God beside me”. Some set themselves up as gods, and some create gods in their minds and as idols, but there is none with him. “I form the light, and create darkness: I make peace, and create evil: I the Lord do all these things”.

Exodus 15:3 fills in the picture: “The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name”. The same Lord that forms the light, creates darkness, makes peace and creates evil is also a man of war. That is the overall picture of the Lord our God.

Psalms 46 shows what that looks like: “Come, behold the works of the Lord, what desolations he hath made in the earth”. Pharaohs were worshipped as gods, Xerxes thought he was a god, and Antiochus Epiphanes thought he was God manifest on earth; rulers rise in power and rise in pride. But “He maketh wars to cease unto the end of the earth; he breaketh the bow, and cutteth the spear in sunder”. The man on the thumbnail who has claimed for two years that he will stop the war between Ukraine and Russia has not stopped anything. When the Iron Dome in Israel failed and the rockets came through, that was no technical glitch; the Lord ripped it open. He makes the prideful instruments of man fail, because he decides where war happens and when it ceases.

And that God of war, who formed the light and created darkness, is Christ. He is our refuge, and he teaches his soldiers to do the same: “Blessed be the Lord my strength, which teacheth my hands to war, and my fingers to fight”. He handpicked us to be soldiers in his army.

precepts.label: Amos 1:13-15
precepts.why:
“Hath Israel no sons? hath he no heir? why then doth their king inherit Gad, and his people dwell in his cities?” Historically, when Gad was moved out of the land, Ammon moved their rusty butts into our land and dwelt in our cities. Amos tells what Ammon did to get there: “For three transgressions of the children of Ammon, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they have ripped up the women with child of Gilead, that they might enlarge their border.”

When they caught our people, they ripped up the women with child. They hung them upside down, just like the white man did to us, cut their stomachs so the baby fell out, and crushed the babies. That is what the Bible says they did, and why: they wanted to enlarge their border and take over our lands. They slaughtered Gad. God says, I'm not forgiving you for that; I'm not letting you slide.

“But I will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabbah, and it shall devour the palaces thereof, with shouting in the day of battle, with a tempest in the day of the whirlwind.” Rabbah is the city of Jeremiah 49:2, where the Lord will cause “an alarm of war” to be heard. A day of battle is coming, with a tempest in the day of the whirlwind: that's the Lord.

“And their king shall go into captivity, he and his princes together, saith the Lord.” Put the leader of North Korea, Kim Jong-un, on the screen. Whether it is that particular man or not, whoever is the leader in the land of Ammon at that time is going to be a prisoner of war. That is what the prophecy says, so look for it.

precepts.label: Romans 8:17
precepts.why:
“then shall Israel be heir unto them that were his heirs, saith the Lord.” What does that mean? Romans 8 jumps right to it: “And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together.”

We are joint-heirs with Christ. Ammon made itself heir to Gad, inheriting his cities while Israel was carried away. But Israel is the heir of God, and in that day Israel shall be heir unto them that took his inheritance.

The condition is that we suffer with him, that we may also be glorified together. The suffering comes first, the inheritance after, just as Gad lost his cities and the Lord promises to give them back.

precepts.label: Obadiah 1:19
precepts.why:
The prophets show whose the land will be: “And they of the south shall possess the mount of Esau”: we're going to own Esau. “and they of the plain the Philistines”: we're going to own them as well. “and they shall possess the fields of Ephraim, and the fields of Samaria”: we're going to get our lands back. “and Benjamin shall possess Gilead.”

The tribe of Benjamin, God foretells, will dwell in the land of Gilead. That is the land of Gad and Reuben and half of Manasseh, the same Gilead whose women with child Ammon ripped up to enlarge their border.

So the prophecy says God is going to give that land in the future to Benjamin. That is Israel being “heir unto them that were his heirs”: the land Ammon took is given back to Israel.

precepts.label: Numbers 32:29
precepts.why:
Before Obadiah's prophecy, the history of the land: when we entered the land, Moses already had it mapped out for us. “If the children of Gad and the children of Reuben will pass with you over Jordan, every man armed to battle, before the Lord, and the land shall be subdued before you; then ye shall give them the land of Gilead for a possession.”

So you notice: Gad and Reuben, that was to be their land. Gilead was Gad's by the word of Moses. That is why Jeremiah asks, “why then doth their king inherit Gad”: the land was Israel's possession, given before the Lord, and Ammon had no right to it.

precepts.label: Numbers 32:39

That conversion is what makes the rest of the verse possible: “that your sins may be blotted out”, forgotten, washed away, “when the times of refreshing shall come from the presence of the Lord.” The times of refreshing are the times of the kingdom being brought upon the earth, when the earth is refreshed.

Ezekiel shows what repentance means in the Old Testament, read right alongside it: “Therefore I will judge you, O house of Israel, every one according to his ways, saith the Lord God. Repent, and turn yourselves from all your transgressions.” When you repent, you turn away from your transgressions. You turn from sin, and the perfect law of the Lord is what turns you and changes your soul.

God is a God of those that repent, as Manasseh found. He did not call the righteous but sinners to repentance, and the way a sinner is converted is by coming under the law of the Lord.

The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 3:18-20
precepts.why:
Paul says “not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but to think soberly”. If God is revealing himself to you, and he doesn't deal with everybody, you had better have some humbleness, because that is the King of kings, the omnipotent Most High God.

Solomon shows why: “I said in mine heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts.” We are all beasts. Although we may be the sons and daughters of God, at the same time we are still beasts in his eyes.

“For that which befalleth the sons of men befalleth beasts; even one thing befalleth them: as the one dieth, so dieth the other”. The lion, the bug that has no value in the eyes of God and just serves the purpose it was created for: we die just like them. “yea, they have all one breath; so that a man hath no preeminence above a beast: for all is vanity.” This is Solomon, the wisest man ever to walk the earth besides Jesus the Christ, saying you have no preeminence above a beast.

So who are you to think you are better than that, to reject what God has written and do as thou wilt? Break it down to its lowest form, and we perish just like everything else. That is where humbleness comes in. We came here and we are going to leave here, so apply these excellent things to your life before you go back to your Maker.

precepts.label: Psalms 82:6-7
precepts.why:
“I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.” That's why we say it: the Israelites are gods upon this earth, children of the Most High.

But read on: “But ye shall die like men, and fall like one of the princes.” We die just like men, just like the beasts of Ecclesiastes 3. In the grand scheme of things, we have no more power over death than the animals do. Are we higher up on the ladder of God's creation? Sure we are. But we perish just like everything else he has created.

That is exactly why a man must not think of himself more highly than he ought to think. Being called gods and children of the Most High is no ground for pride, because the same ones called gods fall like the princes. Think soberly: the one who knows he will die like men humbles himself before the God who made him.

precepts.label: Psalms 90:10
precepts.why:
“The days of our years are threescore years and ten”: seventy years is what we have. “and if by reason of strength they be fourscore years”: if God is merciful, we might get eighty years out of this body. You know the Bible is a true book: you get to hitting around forty and you say, damn, David was right.

That's why Captain Gideon did the class about working out, not drinking sodas and calcifying the bones, eating once a day and taking good care of yourself, so God can be merciful: he did real good with that temple I gave him; let me give him eighty years.

“yet is their strength labour and sorrow; for it is soon cut off, and we fly away.” We fly away means the spirit goes back to its Creator. That is the one day a man is going to fly: when he gets up out of this body.

And even eighty years is nothing to God. Peter says one day with the Lord is as a thousand years; by that measure a whole human lifetime is less than two hours in God's eyes, and it could be even less. Your life is but a vapor. So how do you look down on others and think so highly of yourself? Think soberly, and humble yourself.

precepts.label: Sirach 14:17-19
precepts.why:
“All flesh waxeth old as a garment: for the covenant from the beginning is, Thou shalt die the death.” That is what we just read in David: seventy, maybe eighty years. That is the covenant God pronounced from the beginning: thou shalt die the death.

“As of the green leaves on a thick tree, some fall, and some grow; so is the generation of flesh and blood, one cometh to an end, and another is born.” That is why we have kids. You watch them grow up, and you say, man, I'm getting old. You know the covenant God pronounced upon all flesh, and you are about to cross it too.

“Every work rotteth and consumeth away, and the worker thereof shall go withal.” That is the covenant: thou shalt die the death, thus saith the Lord. Everything a man builds goes with him. So there is no room to think of yourself more highly than you ought; think soberly, knowing the covenant is coming for you like every other leaf on the tree.

precepts.label: Romans 6:23
precepts.why:
Why do we die? We try to break it down so the new people coming into the faith can put the puzzle together: “For the wages of sin is death”. That is why the covenant, thou shalt die the death, passed upon all of us. When Adam listened to his wife Eve and consented to the idolatry she brought to him, sin came into the world, and when sin came, death came with it.

“but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.” That is what we get in the repentance. But we still have to go through the covenant of all flesh. You can't receive the gift of eternal life while you are still in the flesh; flesh and blood cannot enter into the kingdom of heaven. We have to pass through that covenant.

And one thing we had better make sure we don't have on us when we leave this body is pride. That will keep us out of it for sure. That is why Paul says not to think of yourself more highly than you ought: the one who dies like the beasts receives the gift only through Christ, and only if he goes to his grave humble.

“There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able”. The Lord still gives you enough strength not to be overtaken, and always a way out. But it is up to you. Sometimes we are weak in the faith and weak in the spirit: you don't read your four chapters a day, your conversation is not about the scriptures, you are not around the brothers, and Satan gets a hold of you.

When we do not study, we have nothing in our spirits to combat Satan; we are defenseless. Even Christ, when he was tempted, used the word of God: as it is written. We have to be the same way. That is how you combat the lust, the demon: you have to have something in your spirit.

When you go before the magistrates you are told not to think about what you will say, but you still have to have something in your spirit for the Lord to work with. If you have no scriptures about lust in your head, where are you going to pull from? Give the Holy Spirit something to work with. When Joseph, our forefather in Egypt, was tempted, he went straight back to the law: I would be sinning against God. That came to his mind first because his mind was always on the scriptures. precepts.label: Psalms 18:20-23
precepts.why:
Paul forgives “Lest Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his devices.” So examine yourself: has Satan been using some form of pride to hold you back and keep you down? It may be subtle: not asking for help, thinking too highly of yourself, I'm good, I'm fine. Satan has many devices and can transform himself into an angel of light. Captain Matthew put it plainly: fat brothers are too prideful, and that is why they won't change their eating habits.

David shows the other way. “The Lord rewarded me according to my righteousness; according to the cleanness of my hands hath he recompensed me. For I have kept the ways of the Lord, and have not wickedly departed from my God. For all his judgments were before me, and I did not put away his statutes from me.” We all know David committed adultery and put out a hit on a brother. So what does it mean that he did not put away his statutes?

When Nathan the prophet brought it to him, he said, that's me. God was going to take away the child; he fasted and prayed, and when it happened he washed his face, ate bread and said it was the Lord's judgment. He was not prideful. He did not say, I'm the king, I can have as many women as I want, God chose me. He acknowledged his sin, humbled himself and did not put the judgments away.

“I was also upright before him, and I kept myself from mine iniquity.” He went on forward and walked in the ways of the Lord, to the point where God said David is a man after my own heart, because he humbled himself when his sins were brought to him. That is how you keep Satan from getting an advantage of you.

precepts.label: Proverbs 29:23
precepts.why:
Look what pride does: “A man’s pride shall bring him low: but honour shall uphold the humble in spirit.” Pride is one of Satan's devices, and it does not have to be loud and in your face. It can be subtle. Sometimes it shuts you down, I can do this on my own, I don't need anybody, and it always points the finger at somebody else and never at yourself. Pride destroyed us in the kingdom, and it can keep destroying us right now.

Pride destroyed every kingdom on the earth. The king of Assyria sent his messenger with big words against Hezekiah and the Lord, and the angel of the Lord smote a hundred fourscore and five thousand in one night; then his own sons killed Sennacherib with the sword while he worshipped his god. Nebuchadnezzar said, is not this great Babylon, built by the might of my power, and while the word was in his mouth the kingdom departed from him, and he ate grass as oxen until he knew that the Most High ruleth in the kingdom of men. Antiochus spoke proudly and was smitten with a remedyless pain of the bowels. Herod took the glory of a god and was eaten of worms.

No kingdom is exempt, not Assyria, Babylon, Greece, Rome or America. And none is more prideful than Edom, the white man, of whom it is written, the pride of thine heart hath deceived thee.

But honour upholds the humble in spirit. Nebuchadnezzar humbled himself and came back saying there is no God like the God of Daniel. David humbled himself and God called him a man after his own heart. The only way our kingdom will last forever is to walk in wisdom and humility towards God; outside of that, pride brings us low like every nation before us.

precepts.why:
“But the fruit of the Spirit is love”: keeping the commandments. Joy: do you have joy in keeping God's commandments, or are you always sad and depressed? Peace with your wife and with the brothers and sisters, not always arguing and fighting. Longsuffering is patience. Peter shows the same fruits: “And beside this, giving all diligence, add to your faith virtue; and to virtue knowledge”. Knowledge means learning the scriptures and learning how to break them down, because we are not going to be on social media all the time. All of these are the fruits your tree must bring forth.

“For if these things be in you, and abound, they make you that ye shall neither be barren nor unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.” Abound means they stay in you. These things can be in you and then leave you. A brother or sister can be among us six or seven years, growing, the leaves green, and then somebody offends them and all of a sudden they stop bearing fruit.

“But he that lacketh these things is blind, and cannot see afar off, and hath forgotten that he was purged from his old sins.” So examine yourself: am I bearing good fruit? The Lord does not tell you how long he will be patient. A fig tree that bears no fruit is cut down, and a branch that does not abide in Christ withers and is cast into the fire.

precepts.label: Joshua 1:8
precepts.why:
“he that soweth to the Spirit shall of the Spirit reap life everlasting.” When you sow yourself into the scriptures, the Lord is going to give you blessings: he will show you favor, have mercy on you, and give you abundance. That is Joshua 1:8: “This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night.”

We should meditate on the scriptures day and night, “that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.” Meditating and doing is the sowing.

When we do that, the Lord makes our way prosperous. He gives us the abundance we desire, spiritually, emotionally, all the increases we desire, when we put our mind on the Lord. That is reaping of the Spirit.

precepts.label: Romans 6:23
precepts.why:
“whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.” What you put in, you are going to reap. When you put in the sin, the consequences are going to happen, period. Paul says it plainly: “For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.”

Sin is death. That is the corruption reaped by the one who sows to his flesh: sow that sin to your flesh and you will be judged by it. And the gift of God, eternal life through Christ, is the “life everlasting” reaped by the one who sows to the Spirit.

What you put in, you are going to receive as a reward. Wages for sin, a gift for the one who sows to the Spirit. God is not mocked.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 30:19
precepts.why:
The Lord set both harvests before Israel from the beginning: “I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live.”

What you put in, you are going to get; you are going to receive a reward. Life and blessing for the one who sows to the Spirit, death and cursing for the one who sows to his flesh. Heaven and earth are called as witnesses, so no one can say he was not told. God is not mocked.

And the choice reaches past you: choose life “that both thou and thy seed may live.” What a man sows, his children reap with him.

precepts.label: Joshua 24:15
precepts.why:
“And if it seem evil unto you to serve the Lord, choose you this day whom ye will serve.” You cannot serve two masters. You can't serve the flesh and serve God at the same time. You have to choose; ain't no in between.

That is why he said he would rather you be cold or hot. If you are lukewarm, battling that middle ground and playing games, he will spew you out of his mouth. Sowing to the flesh and sowing to the Spirit cannot be done at once.

“whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the flood, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.” Choose the Lord, sow to the Spirit, and of the Spirit reap life everlasting.

precepts.label: Acts 3:19
precepts.why:
“That ye put off concerning the former conversation the old man, which is corrupt according to the deceitful lusts”. The former conversation is the ways of this world, the love of this world. The old man, or old woman, is corrupt and filthy in the eyesight of the Lord, and that mentality manifests itself all the time. The ways of this world are deceitful lusts, hooks in your spirit that will take your soul out of the game. “And be renewed in the spirit of your mind”: by the scriptures. There must be change. That old man must be killed. If you are still the same three or four years in this truth, brothers and sisters, you need to really examine yourself; something is not right.

Acts shows the difference: “Repent ye therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out”. First repent: you stop your sin, you stop breaking the laws of God. Then be converted, which is the actions behind that. You have to have a pattern of righteousness to follow, a pattern of good works, not dabbling in your old sin.

You used to lie; you used to steal. You are not doing those any more. But now what are you doing? You are speaking uprightly to your brothers. You are working, because now you need a manner of provision to provide not only for yourself and your family but for your nation that depends on you. That is the converted part: the works that follow repentance, showing that you truly repented and are no longer that old man or that old woman.

So “put on the new man, which after God is created in righteousness and true holiness.” Put on the king that you are, and sisters, the attributes of your foremothers, the daughters of Sarah. Put away lying, “Let him that stole steal no more: but rather let him labour”, and let no corrupt communication proceed out of your mouth. If you are not investing in the scriptures, the old man will come out in wickedness.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 2:1-5
precepts.why:
“Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life.” You are going to be tried. Sirach tells you to get ready for it: “My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.” You are going to be tempted by Satan; he is going to use devices to tempt you.

“Set thy heart aright”: get your damn mind right, get yourself together, because this is not going to be a fair fight, and it is not going to be easy. “and constantly endure”: you have to constantly endure these temptations, because you have demons in you that you need to purge off, and some of these things keep coming back, and you have to be able to fight and get away from them. Paul in Romans 7 asked the Lord to take it away, and the Lord said no, this is the thorn in your side; this is what you will have to battle. But on the flip side, dealing with those battles is what keeps us going in this truth: always trying to get better with our lives, how we communicate, how we deal in relationships and with one another.

“and make not haste in time of trouble.” Things are going to happen, and you can’t fold up; go full-fledged toward it and knock it out. Life is a fight, and everybody is not going to make it victorious and on top. “Cleave unto him, and depart not away, that thou mayest be increased at thy last end. Whatsoever is brought upon thee take cheerfully, and be patient when thou art changed to a low estate. For gold is tried in the fire.”

You are going to be tried, so make sure you are on point. Everything in the world is against the person trying to be righteous: the work schedule set up to keep you in sin on the weekend, the holidays you want off based on wickedness. So you have to be around righteous people who will hold you accountable. That is the man who endures temptation and receives the crown of life.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 4:1
precepts.why:
“But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” Enticed means there is some attraction there, something that makes us gravitate toward the elements in us that cause us to sin. It seduces us: it looks like it is right for us, but it is not. Paul warned of it: “Now the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits.”

A seducing spirit looks like it is good for you, but it is going to destroy you. Like drugs: that crack feels real good to the crackhead, but he is not able to see around him, and his whole life is being destroyed.

The only way you are going to see whether it is good for you or not is by filtering it through the scriptures. That is why it is important to be studying, reading your four chapters, being around godly men and godly women, so somebody can have your back. You have to be in the spirit to discern whether a thing is righteousness or Satan’s kiss.

Temptation begins internally; the lust is in you. When temptation presents itself you begin to be drawn to it, sin starts enticing you, and it grows through agreement: you get enticed, then you agree with it. “Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death.” It becomes action, and it always ends in destruction. “There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death.” In your own counsel you will always think you are right, and that is how people give heed to seducing spirits and depart from the faith.

precepts.label: 1 John 2:15
precepts.why:
“From whence come wars and fightings among you? come they not hence, even of your lusts that war in your members?” It is a consistent battle between the spiritual man and the carnal man. “Ye lust, and have not: ye kill, and desire to have”: you slander the brother or sister who has what you want, give them the evil eye, speak nasty. You ask for a home, a car, a wife, and receive not, because you “ask amiss, that ye may consume it upon your lusts”: to show off, to stunt, to have a trophy wife, to be seen of men.

Christ said if you love the world, you hate me. John writes it: “Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world. If any man love the world, the love of the Father is not in him.” Love not this captivity, neither the precious things and riches in this captivity, neither the mansion on the hill, not even your damn job. A lot of brothers love their jobs more than they love this truth.

These things are hooks inside of you that will pull you out of this truth. They are devices of Satan, the tangible trinkets he gives, which our brothers and sisters lust after as status symbols when the kingdom of heaven is at hand. In Babylon everything is accessible at your fingertips, and everything as far as your eye can see appeals to the flesh.

If any man loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him. That is why James says “the friendship of the world is enmity with God.” Enmity means the state of being actively opposed or hostile, a feud, conflict, bitterness, resentment. That is the mentality that says why do I have to keep the Sabbath, I could be at home, the boxing match is on today. Some sneak off for Christmas and come back with fifteen presents in the trunk. You hate God and God’s laws. This captivity, the dominion of your oppressor, is going to go, and if you don’t kill that old man and that old woman, you are going with him. Kill or be killed.

precepts.label: Matthew 6:24
precepts.why:
On the line of adultery and lust and the love of the world, Christ said: “No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.”

A decision has to be made. Either you hate God, have enmity against him, and love the other, or you hold to the one and despise the other. The other can be money, your career, your bed because you don’t want to be here, a Christmas stocking full of abominations. Some snuck off and celebrated the devastation of their brothers, the slaughter of the tribe of Gad, got a turkey drumstick, watched the football game, then came back saying shalom, Most High in Christ bless. Many will hold on to the world and despise the heavenly Father.

You cannot serve the God of the nation of Israel and mammon. Brothers and sisters are more loyal to their jobs and the white man who runs the corporations, who can terminate your contract after fifteen years of loyalty just as you are getting ready to retire. That is serving mammon.

James calls it what it is: “Ye adulterers and adulteresses.” When these other things have become a god, you have committed adultery against the heavenly Father. Many do not hate the world; they hate having to change and repent. That is the war in your members, and you have to kill that adulterous spirit inside you or it will kill you.

precepts.label: Ephesians 5:26
precepts.why:
God “resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble.” The humble submit to God and resist the devil, and James goes on: “Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.” How do we purify our minds? Paul shows how Christ cleanses his people: “That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word.”

In Christianity many think that because they dipped themselves in water they are a whole other person. But the true baptism is washing yourself with the word. Sitting here in the class, hearing the scriptures, is that washing. And to sanctify and cleanse by the washing of water by the word means you have to keep the commandments. That is the way you cleanse yourself.

The hands are cleansed of your evil works and evil ways, and the heart is purified of the old worldly mindset. The double minded are the brothers who want to be here but do not want to be here, one foot in and one foot out the door. That is lukewarm, and the Lord will spew the lukewarm out, which means he will put you to death. So either you are hot and kill that old man with the word, or you are lukewarm and you will be killed. Either way, somebody has to die.

The humble who receive that grace are the ones taking steps to kill the old man, sharpening their swords with the word to subdue the evil spirit that plagued them for years before they knew this glorious gospel. That washing is how the Lord draws nigh to them.

precepts.label: Psalms 19:7
precepts.why:
James says God “giveth grace unto the humble”, and calls on them: “Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.” Paul says Christ cleanses his people “with the washing of water by the word.” David shows what that word is and what it does: “The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.”

The law of the Lord is perfect, and that is what is going to cleanse you. That is what makes you perfect. Keeping the commandments is the cleansing. It converts the soul: it turns the old man into a new man, and makes the simple wise.

That is how you purify your mind. Remove from you the old ways, the old worldly mindset. You cannot get that cleansing from the white man's couch or from cashing a check; pay all the bills and you will still feel empty without the Lord in your life. Submit yourselves to his will, to his law, statutes and commandments, and resist the devil, the deceiver: his lies, the Trinity, the apologetics, the false doctrines of the other nations, and the world, point blank, period.

The more you apply the law and read, the more the Lord draws nigh to you and opens his understanding to you: the dark mysteries and the parables, how to guide your household, and how to stand in the temptations, trials and lusts that come your way. The perfect law is the weapon that kills the old man.

precepts.why:
God “delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked”. Examine yourself: are you vexed with the filthy conversation of this world? Or are you up late scrolling, looking at booties, two hours in the middle of the night on your phone? Those two hours you could have read the Bible. But to be vexed, you have to be in this Bible. It is by having the word of God in you that sin starts becoming repulsive. If you are not reading and not studying, the sins of the world will be normal to you, just like everybody else. The Lord saved a remnant, and that is why we did not become as Sodom and Gomorrha. What is that remnant doing? Studying day and night.

Paul and Silas were sent by night unto Berea and went into the synagogue, and “These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.” If you are searching the scriptures daily, you will be vexed with the filthy conversation of this world. If you are not, whose words are going to be in your ears? The TV, the street, your phone: the ways of this world.

God turned Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes, “making them an ensample unto those that after should live ungodly”. America read the example and legalized gay marriage anyway, a habitual line stepper pushing the envelope until his sin reached the heavens. Only the one searching the scriptures daily will be vexed like Lot and delivered like Lot.
